Its strength is graded by glyph, strongest (0.5-1.0 of max) for the dash/slash/joiner family ' -', ' –', ' —', ' /', ' ·', ' |', ' >', ' --', ' +', ' •', ' :', ' ||', ' //' (and rarer forms such as ' ›', ' ―', ' ..', ' ---'), moderate (about 0.25-0.5 of max, sometimes just under the active threshold) for a detached ampersand, question or exclamation mark, semicolon, asterisk, equals sign, ellipsis or period, and at or below the active threshold for a detached comma, close paren, open bracket, quote, dollar sign, hash or backtick; the same glyph without its leading space (bare '-', '–', '/', as in 'well-known', '1925–2013', 'http://', 'Key:') is not detected at all. It is retrospective: the peak lands on the separator itself (76% of the input attribution is on that token), the token that follows it has no effect, the Jacobian-lens write just mirrors the same detached-glyph family (' >', ' ►', ' ..', ' ›', ' =>', ' :') and the measured ablation profile is unconcentrated (KL 0.006) - and it is about three times weaker when the separator starts a line after a newline (0.3-0.6) or about 40% weaker after another space-prefixed punctuation token (~1.0-1.2) than when it follows the last letter or digit of the left-hand item (1.4-2.0), which drops the weaker glyphs below the active threshold at a line start.
